findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body: Every call to `recordIssuedToken` passes the raw token to `audit`, which writes it to `console.log`. Where console output is retained or aggregated, log readers can recover and reuse an unexpired bearer credential. Record only non-sensitive metadata.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from a login parameter, passing it directly to `location.assign` permits attacker-controlled absolute URLs and potentially unsafe schemes. Validate that the destination is an intended same-origin URL before navigating.

findings.title: [P2] Validate the cache entry before calling trim
findings.body: For an absent key inherited from `Object.prototype`, such as `cachedName({}, "toString")`, the lookup obtains a function and invokes its nonexistent `trim` method, throwing instead of returning the fallback. Check for an own string value before trimming.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every call to `recordIssuedToken` passes the raw token to `console.log`. In deployments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover bearer credentials and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin destinations
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` is derived from a login query parameter or other untrusted input, values such as `https://attacker.example/phish` redirect authenticated users off-site, creating an open-redirect/phishing vector.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Check for an own string value before trimming the cache entry
findings.body:
A normal object cache with an absent key that matches an inherited property now throws. For example, `cachedName({}, "toString")` obtains `Object.prototype.toString` and attempts to call its nonexistent `trim` method, producing a `TypeError` instead of the fallback. User-controlled keys can therefore fail requests.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin destinations
findings.body:
`finishLogin` now accepts any URL and navigates to it. If an attacker controls `returnUrl` (for example, `https://attacker.example/phish`), a trusted login flow becomes an open redirect; dangerous schemes such as `javascript:` may also execute in permissive browser/CSP environments.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Stop writing issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is logged in plaintext. In deployments where console output is retained or forwarded, anyone with broader log access can recover and reuse an unexpired bearer token.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
